title: Every customer you don't answer goes to someone else.
intro: Your hands are full: cutting, installing, serving. The customer does not wait: they call the next business on the list. This is what tends to happen at a Hialeah business.
calls_title: The phone rings and you can't pick up
calls_body: You're with a client in the chair, or up on a roof. The call is missed and nobody leaves a message. Someone shopping for a service calls several places; the one who answers first gets the job.
calls_cost: A missed call is a customer who doesn't call back.
phone_scene: The customer is on their phone
phone_title: Your site doesn't work well on a phone
phone_body: Tiny text, buttons that don't respond, or a page that takes a while to open. Most people look you up on their phone, on the street or on the couch. If it's hard to read, they leave.
phone_cost: If it doesn't work on a phone, they never get as far as calling you.
language_title: No Spanish, or no easy way to write to you
language_body: In Hialeah some customers ask for everything in Spanish and others in English. If your page is in one language, or has no form and no clear way to ask for a price, many are left not knowing how to reach you.
language_cost: Someone who can't follow the page, or can't find how to write to you, doesn't contact you.
bridge: You do not need to learn anything about technology. See below how it works with a pretend business, and try it yourself.
